info.long_name: Number of NAAT tests performed by participating commercial laboratories (COVID-19)
info.short_description: Weekly count of COVID-19 NAAT tests
info.long_description: Weekly count of nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) for COVID-19 reported by participating commercial laboratories (Labcorp, Quest, Aegis, ARUP, Perimeter), by state of patient residence (or ordering provider). Counts are specimens, not unique persons. Counts under 10 are suppressed (NA); zeros are not. National (geography 00) is the sum of state counts for each week.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} COVID-19 tests were performed by commercial laboratories in the week ending {time}.

info.long_name: Number of NAAT tests performed by participating commercial laboratories (flu)
info.short_description: Weekly count of flu NAAT tests
info.long_description: Weekly count of nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) for flu reported by participating commercial laboratories (Labcorp, Quest, Aegis, ARUP, Perimeter), by state of patient residence (or ordering provider). Counts are specimens, not unique persons. Counts under 10 are suppressed (NA); zeros are not. National (geography 00) is the sum of state counts for each week.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} flu tests were performed by commercial laboratories in the week ending {time}.

Counts are specimens, not unique persons. Counts under 10 are suppressed (NA); zeros are not. National (geography 00) is the sum of state counts for each week.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} RSV tests were performed by commercial laboratories in the week ending {time}.

info.long_name: Number of positive NAAT tests from commercial laboratories (COVID-19)
info.short_description: Weekly count of positive COVID-19 tests
info.long_description: Weekly count of positive NAATs for COVID-19. CDC suppresses counts under 10; where tests were performed but positives were suppressed, the positive count is imputed as 5 (the midpoint of 0-9) and the suppression flag is 1. Zeros are not suppressed. National (geography 00) is the sum of state counts for each week, so it includes the imputed 5s from suppressed states and is approximate; the suppression flag is NA for national.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} commercial lab COVID-19 tests were positive in the week ending {time}.

info.long_name: Number of positive NAAT tests from commercial laboratories (flu)

info.long_description: Weekly count of positive NAATs for flu. info.statement: In {location}, {value} commercial lab flu tests were positive in the week ending {time}.

National (geography 00) is the sum of state counts for each week, so it includes the imputed 5s from suppressed states and is approximate; the suppression flag is NA for national.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} commercial lab RSV tests were positive in the week ending {time}.

info.long_name: Percent of NAAT tests that were positive in commercial laboratories (COVID-19)
info.short_description: Weekly percent positivity of COVID-19 NAAT tests
info.long_description: Positive NAATs divided by NAATs classified as positive or negative, times 100. Where positives were suppressed (under 10), percent positivity is recomputed from the imputed positive count of 5 divided by the test count, times 100, and the suppression flag is 1. Not a representative sample; geographic coverage varies by laboratory. National (geography 00) is total positives divided by total tests across states, times 100; because it includes imputed positives from suppressed states it is affected by state-level suppression.
info.statement: In {location}, {value}% of commercial lab COVID-19 tests were positive in the week ending {time}.

info.long_name: Positive count and percent positivity suppressed (COVID-19)
info.short_description: 1 if COVID-19 tests were performed but positives/percent were suppressed
info.long_description: Equals 1 when the test count is > 0 but the positive count is missing because of CDC small-number suppression (<10); the positive count is then imputed as 5 and percent positivity recomputed from it. Otherwise 0. For national (geography 00), which is the sum of states, the flag is NA, because some state is suppressed in nearly every week and the flag would not be informative; the national values include imputed positives from suppressed states.

nssp_lab.name: NSSP Commercial Laboratory Data: COVID-19, Flu, and RSV
nssp_lab.location: NSSP Commercial Laboratory Test Volumes and Results by State
nssp_lab.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nssp_lab.description: This dataset provides the percentage of emergency department patient visits for the specified pathogen of all ED patient visits that were observed for the given week from data submitted to the National Syndromic Surveillance Program (NSSP) and weekly state-level NAAT test volumes, positives, and percent positivity for specified pathogens from five commercial laboratories (Labcorp, Quest Diagnostics, Aegis Sciences, ARUP, Perimeter). ED visit data start on 2020-10-01 and lab data start on 2024-10-05. Both are update weekly. State is assigned by patient zip code (or ordering provider's). Note that lab tests are not a representative sample; representation is uneven by region and condition, and prior weeks may be revised. The reported sub-state trends are from Health Service Areas (HSA) and the data reported from the health care facilities located within the given HSA. Health Service Areas are regions of one or more counties that align to patterns of care seeking. The HSA level data are reported for each county in the HSA. Some states report state-level data but not county-level data. In these instances, PopHIVE maps the state-level data to the counties in that state so that all counties in the state share the same value. These data are made available by the CDC.
nssp_lab.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nssp.name: National Syndromic Surveillance Program (NSSP)
nssp.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nssp.description: This dataset provides the percentage of emergency department patient visits for the specified pathogen of all ED patient visits for the specified geographic part of the country that were observed for the given week from data submitted to the National Syndromic Surveillance Program (NSSP). Note that the reported sub-state trends are from Health Service Areas (HSA) and the data reported from the health care facilities located within the given HSA. Health Service Areas are regions of one or more counties that align to patterns of care seeking. The HSA level data are reported for each county in the HSA. Some states report state-level data but not county-level data. In these instances, PopHIVE maps the state-level data to the counties in that state so that all counties in the state share the same value. These data are made available by the CDC.
nssp.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

_catalog.summary: The NSSP records the percentage of emergency department patient visits for RSV, flu, and COVID-19, plus weekly commercial lab test counts and percent positive by state.
